summit.title: Three stars, two singles
summit.story: Girona's starred cooking runs from a three-star house in a suburb to two single stars in town. El Celler de Can Roca opened in 1986 near the Roca parents' bar in Taialà, holds three MICHELIN stars and marked forty years on 5 October 2026 with a menu of forty small dishes. Massana opened on Carrer Bonastruc de Porta the same year, has held a star since 2007 and this spring passed the stoves from Pere Massana to his son Pere. Divinum started as a wine bar on Carrer Argenteria in 2001 and won its star in the 2025 guide in a vault under the old Casino. The 2027 list is announced on 24 November 2026.
summit.where: El Celler de Can Roca, Girona; Massana, Girona; Divinum, Girona

roca.title: Three rungs of Roca
roca.story: The Roca family feeds Girona at three price points. Can Roca, the bar Josep Roca and Montserrat Fontané opened in Taialà in 1967, has long served a cheap weekday menú that El Celler's own brigade eats at lunch; we found nothing dated 2026 for it, so call before crossing town. Normal, on Plaça de l'Oli, has Elisabet Nolla cooking the dishes of the Roca grandmother and mother and holds a Repsol Sol. Up the hill at Sant Julià de Ramis, Esperit Roca serves El Celler's back catalogue inside an 1893 fort: one MICHELIN star since the 2025 guide, menus that turn with the seasons, and eighth place among Europe's new restaurants on the 2026 Opinionated About Dining list.
roca.where: Can Roca, Girona; Normal, Girona; Esperit Roca, Sant Julià de Ramis

houses.title: Family houses, market cooking
houses.story: Girona's long-running tables cook from the market and keep the same dishes for decades. Casa Marieta has served duck with pears on Plaça de la Independència since 1892, run by the fifth generation of one family. Can Marquès opened in 1920 beside the site of the Mercat del Lleó and still sets Thursday aside for a rice made from what the stalls sold. The newest, Fonda Cal Ros, opened in April 2025 under the Voltes d'en Rosés, where the Gascons family of starred Els Tinars pass porrons round, hang tomatoes for bread and serve Torroella de Montgrí cured meats for diners to help themselves.
houses.where: Casa Marieta, Girona; Can Marquès, Girona; Fonda Cal Ros, Girona

chefs.title: The new rooms
chefs.story: Girona's cooks eat in small rooms run by people they trained with. Dit i Fet, below Sant Feliu, is a cook and a host who came out of El Celler cooking old Catalan dishes for about thirty-five covers; its card says who sends you there. SAFO, by Plaça del Vi, pairs Marietta Richter's Mexican and Catalan share plates with Víctor Martín's natural wines, and won the emerging-chef Cuiner award in 2024. The third room comes from further east: Nomo, a Barcelona group with a Tokyo-trained chef-partner, Naoyuki Haginoya, opened in 2021 round the protected garden of the Jardins de la Mercè, a 1900 manor.
chefs.where: Dit i Fet, Girona; SAFO, Girona; Nexe, Girona

menu.title: The working lunch menú
menu.story: In Girona the menú del dia is how offices, shop staff and builders eat at midday: a fixed price, a short choice of firsts and seconds, bread, a drink and dessert. 8de7, on Carrer de les Hortes, has served a closed menú of three firsts and three seconds since late 2014, and spring 2026 diners still mention the queue. Tornés, out on Carrer del Migdia, is a pastisseria founded in 1965 that serves lunch behind the cake counter; dessert is chosen from its own pastry, and in March 2026 its xuixo won the world contest for Girona's own sweet. Both are a walk from the old town, and both fill by half past one.

morning.title: Chocolate, stew and coffee
morning.story: Girona's mornings run on three traditions. The granja serves thick hot chocolate: Xocolateria L'Antiga has poured it under the Plaça del Vi arcades since 1916. The esmorzar de forquilla is a working breakfast of stews eaten with a fork: at Ca l'Àngel, a roadside bar opened in 1978 north of the city at Fontcoberta, cap i pota is on the table from six. The newest is cycling coffee: Christian Meier, a Canadian pro, and his wife Amber opened La Fàbrica on Carrer de la Llebre in 2015, and riders stop there after training. Each fits a different crew: the early starter, the driver heading north, the rest day.
morning.where: Xocolateria L'Antiga, Girona; Ca l'Àngel, Fontcoberta; La Fàbrica, Girona

other.title: Tokyo and Kathmandu, Barri Vell
other.story: Away from Catalan cooking, the old town has a few kitchens from much further east. Nomo, a Barcelona group with a Tokyo-trained chef-partner, Naoyuki Haginoya, opened in 2021 in the Jardins de la Mercè, a 1900 manor whose garden is protected in the city catalogue; diners were reviewing its sushi and tasting menu in June 2026. On Carrer dels Calderers, a small bar named after the lioness column outside, the one visitors kiss to be sure of coming back, says it now cooks Nepali momos and dal bhat alongside Catalan plates, though no outside source confirmed the change. One is a group restaurant, the other a neighbourhood bar.
other.where: Nomo Girona, Girona; El Cul de la Lleona, Girona

sweet.title: Xuixo, chocolate, soft-serve
sweet.story: Girona's own pastry is the xuixo, fried laminated dough rolled in sugar and filled with crema; in 2026 the city and guilds proposed a mark to protect the cream-filled original. Can Castelló, a pastry family since 1898, gave up everything else in 2014 to sell only xuixos from Carrer de l'Argenteria, frying about 5,000 a day in Banyoles. The Roca brothers added two more stops: Jordi Roca's Casa Cacao, opened in February 2020 on Plaça de Catalunya, roasts and conches its own beans under a fifteen-room hotel, and his gelateria Rocambolesc, opened in 2012 on Santa Clara, puts the Celler's dessert ideas into a cone.
sweet.where: Can Castelló, Girona; Casa Cacao, Girona; Rocambolesc, Girona

larder.title: Market, cheese counter, vineyard
larder.story: Provisioning in Girona starts at the Mercat del Lleó, the covered market opened on 3 November 1944; in 2024 the Salvador family, Tossa de Mar fishmongers since 1966, took over the fish stall Peixos Pol had kept for eighty years. Across the river in the Barri Vell, Cal Formatger puts the province's small dairies and a good part of Spain's on one counter; its card has who runs it and who shops there. For wine, the drive is fifty minutes north-east to Vilajuïga, where Anna Espelt farms about 200 organic hectares of DO Empordà, including a Carinyena Blanca vineyard planted in 1919.
larder.where: Mercat del Lleó, Girona; Cal Formatger, Girona; Espelt Viticultors, Vilajuïga

late.title: After service, before midnight
late.story: Girona eats early for Spain and closes early, so a crew finishing late has few choices. Zanpanzar, a Basque pintxo counter on Carrer de la Cort Reial since December 1999, keeps trays moving until midnight and counts the bill by toothpicks. König, which grew from a frankfurt stand Pere Parals opened in 1973, sells more braves than water across its branches according to Ara, and its Calderers terrace serves until about 23:00. After that the music takes over: the Sunset Jazz Club, in a vaulted cellar since November 2001, stays open past one, has no kitchen, and was named by DownBeat among the world's best jazz clubs in 2026.
late.where: Zanpanzar, Girona; König Sandwiches, Girona; Sunset Jazz Club, Girona
